claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Hello! I'd be happy to help you find out if you're eligible for Child Benefit.

To assess your eligibility, I'll need to ask you a few questions about your circumstances.

First, could you please tell me how many children you're looking to claim Child Benefit for, and what are their names and ages?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim for my son Alex. He's 18 years old.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information about Alex.

Since Alex is 18 years old, I need to ask a few more questions to determine eligibility, as the rules are different for children aged 16 and over.

Is Alex currently in approved education or training, such as:
- A-levels or equivalent
- Scottish Highers
- NVQs (up to level 3)
- A traineeship in England

Or has he left education/training?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he's left education. He finished school and isn't studying anything at the moment.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for clarifying that.

Since Alex is 18 and has left education, I need to ask one more question:

Has Alex recently left education or training (within the last 20 weeks)? If so, did he register with the armed services or a careers service, or register for work or training with a qualifying body after leaving?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, he hasn't done any of that. He just left school and hasn't signed up with careers services or anything like that.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Based on the information you've provided and the official eligibility rules, I now have enough information to make a determination about your Child Benefit eligibility for Alex.

Here's what the rules state:
- You normally qualify for Child Benefit if you're responsible for a child **under 16**
- For children aged **16 or over**, you can continue to receive Child Benefit if they stay in **approved education or training** until they turn 20
- For 16 or 17 year olds who leave education, you can apply for Child Benefit to continue for 20 weeks **if they register with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed services**

Since Alex is 18 years old, has left education, and has not registered with a careers service or the armed services, unfortunately he does not meet the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'm sorry to say that based on the information you've provided, **you are not eligible for Child Benefit for Alex**.

**The reason:**
- Alex is 18 years old and has left education
- For children aged 16 or over, Child Benefit can only continue if the child remains in **approved education or training** (such as A-levels, Scottish Highers, or NVQs up to level 3) until they turn 20
- The option to extend Child Benefit for 20 weeks after leaving education by registering with a careers service or the armed services only applies to **16 and 17 year olds**, not to those who are 18

If Alex's circumstances change in the future—for example, if he decides to return to approved education or training—you may become eligible again at that point.

Is there anything else I can help you with?

Since Alex is 18, has left education, and has not registered with any careers service or the armed services, he does not meet any of the eligibility criteria for Child Benefit.
